summary: Bosutinib is an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor of BCR-ABL and Src-family kinases used to treat Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (chronic, accelerated, or blast phase) that is resistant or intolerant to prior therapy. Hallmark toxicities are gastrointestinal (especially diarrhea) and hepatotoxicity, along with myelosuppression, fluid retention, cardiovascular and renal effects. It must be taken with food, and liver enzymes and blood counts require close monitoring.

moa: Bosutinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits the BCR-ABL kinase driving chronic myelogenous leukemia, including many imatinib-resistant BCR-ABL forms (but not the T315I or V299L mutants). It is also an inhibitor of Src-family kinases including Src, Lyn, and Hck. By blocking BCR-ABL signaling it suppresses proliferation of the malignant clone.

absolute: History of hypersensitivity to bosutinib (reactions have included anaphylaxis)
relative: Pre-existing hepatic impairment (reduce dose; hepatotoxicity risk)
Active gastrointestinal disease or fluid overload/heart failure
Pregnancy / women of reproductive potential without contraception
Concurrent strong CYP3A modulators or PPIs

preg: Based on findings in animals and its mechanism, bosutinib can cause fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential of the risk and to use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 1 week after the final dose; avoid use in pregnancy.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for a period after the last dose (per product labeling).
renal: Reduce the dose in patients with moderate to severe renal impairment. For baseline CrCl 30-50 mL/min reduce to about 400 mg once daily, and for CrCl <30 mL/min to about 300 mg once daily. Monitor renal function during therapy.
hepatic: For patients with pre-existing hepatic impairment, reduce the starting dose to 200 mg once daily. Monitor liver enzymes at least monthly for the first 3 months and as clinically needed; withhold, dose-reduce, or discontinue for hepatotoxicity.

major: Strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, etc.) - markedly increase bosutinib exposure; avoid
Strong/moderate CYP3A inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine) - markedly decrease exposure; avoid
Proton pump inhibitors (reduce bosutinib absorption via increased gastric pH); avoid
moderate: H2-receptor antagonists / antacids (reduce absorption - separate dosing)
P-glycoprotein substrates (bosutinib may increase their levels)

interactions.alcohol: Avoid heavy alcohol use given hepatotoxicity potential
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver transaminases and bilirubin, complete blood counts, serum creatinine, and lipase

counsel: Take with food and swallow tablets whole at the same time each day
Diarrhea is common - stay hydrated and report severe or persistent diarrhea promptly
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, unusual bruising or bleeding, fever, or swelling/shortness of breath
Do not use antacids/heartburn medicines near your dose without advice; avoid grapefruit
Use effective contraception during and after treatment; do not breastfeed
Keep appointments for blood and liver tests

pearls: Inactive against the T315I and V299L BCR-ABL mutations - genotype before relying on it for resistant disease
Diarrhea is the most common adverse effect, usually early and manageable
Hepatotoxicity warrants monthly liver enzyme checks for the first 3 months
Food increases absorption; proton pump inhibitors substantially reduce it

missed: If a dose is missed and more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take the next usual prescribed dose the following day. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience. Patients who take more than the prescribed dose should be observed and given supportive care; monitor for exaggerated adverse effects (GI toxicity, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, fluid retention). There is no specific antidote.
